expectedMisconceptions: Children can treat one source (usually the rock samples, since they're the most tangible) as sufficient on its own, rather than combining samples, layers and maps together — the mission's own assessment specifically calls for evidence 'from the samples, layers and maps together, not just one source.'
A field sketch can end up decorative rather than informative if it isn't labelled — a pretty drawing isn't the same as a useful one.
stretchQuestions: Which single piece of evidence — samples, layers, or maps — was most convincing on its own, and which needed the others to make sense?
How might disturbing the survey area, rather than just observing it, have changed what future Explorers could learn?
estimatedSupervision: Light — real rocks or stones can help if available, per the mission's own parent guide, but nothing is required.
